one_month_reasoning: No PANW earnings in the window (to Nov 5). Q1 FY27 ends Oct 31. As of Oct 5 the company has filed no 8-K giving a date; its recent filings are Forms 4/144 [3]. Last year the Q1 date was announced on Nov 4, 2025 for a Nov 19 report [4]. A report before Nov 5 would need results within 5 days of quarter-end, so it is effectively ruled out. If the date announcement falls in the window, it carries no information. Scheduled macro: the Oct 27-28 FOMC [34], where Kalshi/Polymarket price ~84% hold and ~16% a 25bp hike as of Oct 6 [35]. A hike would hit a ~97x NTM P/E name hardest. That is context only, not a directional call. Short-horizon regularities: the stock closed at an all-time high of $419.91 (+3.2% on the day, intraday $432.33) after a +27.8% run from the $328.48 post-earnings close on Sep 2 [8]. Momentum and short-term reversal roughly offset, so I make no drift call. I centre a lognormal at ~$418, a hair below spot to allow for the Oct 6 intraday fade. Monthly sigma is 14.5%: between 47.4% 1Y realized / 3.5 = 13.5% and 57.7% 3M realized / 3.5 = 16.5% (the trailing-year 21-day log-return s.d. is 16.0%) [8]. Valuation (fair value $258) is not allowed to move a 1-month forecast.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend at the Oct-2027 horizon. P/E: 52x (10-peer calendar-weighted NTM median 50.3x, +3%) x Oct-2027 NTM consensus non-GAAP EPS $5.01 = $260.4. EV/FCF: the 10-peer trailing EV/FCF median of 41.3x x FY27 FCF on the same GAAP-style basis, $5.01B (38% x $14.15B guide x 0.931 SA/adjusted conversion) = EV $206.7B, + net cash $11.14B ($6.13B + FY27 FCF), / 850M shares = $256.3. Blend $258.3. The round-1 Goldman price-drift anchor is removed.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 (Aug-2027 to Jul-2028) is ~82% of the 12 months after Oct 6, 2027: 0.82 x 4.881 + 0.18 x 5.583 = $5.007. The same method today gives NTM $4.314 and 97.3x at $419.91, consistent with SA's 97.10x forward PE [6].

Each peer: NTM EPS = w x current-FY consensus EPS (SA forecast page) + (1-w) x current FY x (1 + SA 3Y EPS CAGR), with w = share of the current fiscal year left after Oct 6, 2026 (0.25 Dec FYE, 1/3 Jan FYE, 0.82 Jul FYE). P/E = Oct 6 close / NTM EPS. Median of FTNT 49.5, SAIL 51.1 = 50.3x. See comps.

2025 average month-end close $190.98 (Twelve Data monthly) / FY26 non-GAAP EPS $3.84 = 49.7x, roughly the forward multiple on the fiscal year then in progress. Corroborates the peer median as a level PANW itself traded at before the 2026 AI-security re-rating.

Peer median 50.3x +3%. For a premium: the FY27 NGS ARR guide of +22-23% is essentially organic, because both big deals closed before FY27 [1]. Against it, the peer 3Y revenue CAGR median is 15.3% [11-20]. RPO is $21.2B, +34% [1], and Q3 organic revenue growth was +14.2% = (3,002-388)/2,289-1 [2]. Against a premium: PANW's 3Y EPS CAGR of 14.4% [6] is below the peer median of 16.3%, SBC is $1.712B (14.9% of FY26 revenue) [1], and PANW's own 2025 multiple was ~49.7x [9]. I can show only a small premium persisting through Oct-2027, so I use a multiple just above the median and well inside the peer range.

bear.story: The AI-security premium unwinds, as in the 2021-22 analog where CRWD/ZS/NET fell 43-71% in the 12 months after their Oct-2021 peak [10]. Rates add pressure (a 16% priced odds of an Oct hike [35]). PANW rerates to 45x Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $5.01 = $225, below the 50.3x peer median as peer multiples also compress. Consensus EPS still holds, so this is a multiple story. It is the level PANW traded at in late May 2026 ($243-248) [8].

base.story: PANW delivers the FY27 guide (revenue $14.10-14.20B, EPS $4.16-4.19, NGS ARR +22-23%) and consensus FY28 (+16.5% EPS) [1,5]. The multiple closes about half the gap between today's 97x and the ~50x peer median, giving ~70x x $5.01 = $350. Headline growth converges to organic as CyberArk laps from Feb-2027, which caps re-rating.

bull.story: AI-driven attack risk keeps security at the top of budgets (management's framing [1]). Organic NGS ARR beats the +22-23% guide, EPS lands ~5% above consensus (~$5.26), and the market keeps ~99x NTM, as CRWD (184x) and NET (222x) do today [12,16]: 99 x 5.26 = ~$520. PANW's own history after +90% years shows next-12m returns up to +93% in 2021 [9].

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Only a small premium (+3%) is argued as persistent. For: the FY27 NGS ARR guide of +22-23% is essentially organic [1], against a peer 3Y revenue CAGR median of 15.3%; RPO is $21.2B (+34%) [1]; and PANW has the largest scale (FY26 revenue $11.48B). Against: PANW's consensus 3Y EPS CAGR of 14.4% is below the peer median of 16.3%, because CyberArk was paid in stock. Q3 FY26 organic revenue growth was +14.2% [2]. SBC is ~15% of revenue [1]. PANW's own 2025 multiple was ~49.7x [9]. No sell-side outperformance view is used. Round 1's 70x relied on 23-24% FY27 revenue growth, which includes ~6 months of acquired revenue, so I withdrew it.

thesis_break_reason: $215 is 43x consensus Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $5.01. That is below the 50.3x peer median, below PANW's own ~49.7x 2025 multiple, and below the 2026-05-27 and 2026-06-09 intraday lows ($243.04 / $251.15) [8,9] (citation gate: these are single-day lows, not the May low, which was $177.41 on 2026-05-01). Multiple normalisation alone takes the stock to my $258 fair value or the $225 bear case. A sustained move to $215 would mean the market is also pricing estimate cuts of ~10-15%: an FY27 NGS ARR or revenue guide cut, the 40% FY28 FCF-margin target [1] withdrawn, or CyberArk/identity slippage. That is fundamental damage, not 47%-vol noise.

Base rates conflict. PANW's own history after +60% trailing years: median next-12m +19.5%, 29% negative (34 overlapping months) [9]. After >90% years: median ~+10.5% (20 months). The 2021 cyber analog: -43% to -71% for CRWD/ZS/NET, but PANW itself was flat (+1%, Oct-21 to Oct-22) [9,10].
Rates: an Oct-2026 hike is priced at ~16% [35]; a 2026 recession at 6.5% on Polymarket ($2.27M volume) [36].
reasoning: Company facts, re-verified at primary sources this round. FY26 revenue $11.48B, FY26 EPS $3.84, adj FCF $4.414B. FY27 guide: revenue $14.10-14.20B, NGS ARR +22-23%, EPS $4.16-4.19, 38% adj FCF margin, 844-847M diluted shares. Targets: 40% adj FCF margin in FY28 and $20B FY30 NGS ARR. Net cash $6.13B [1]. Q3 acquired contributions give organic revenue growth of +14.2% [2]. Consensus: FY27 $4.19 and FY28 +16.48% [5], giving Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $5.01. Valuation is on one consistent basis: the 10-peer calendar-weighted NTM P/E median is 50.3x, and PANW is at 97x. I apply 52x to get $260. The trailing EV/FCF median of 41.3x on SA-basis FY27 FCF gives $256. Fair value is $258, down from $363 in round 1. The supervisor's corrections drive most of the drop: the Goldman anchor is removed and 70x was not justified. The rest is my own basis fix on FCF. I disagree with two supervisor choices. (a) Its +10% premium (55x) is not demonstrably persistent: PANW's EPS growth is below the peer median, and its own verified 2025 multiple was ~49.7x. (b) Its EV/FCF applies a peer multiple on SA (GAAP-style) FCF to PANW's adjusted FCF and blends FY28 into a TTM not yet reported at the horizon. Ladder versus fair value: fair value is where the stock would sit with the premium fully normalised. Twelve months rarely completes that. PANW's own record after big up-years is still positive on median [9]. The 2021 analog shows full or over-normalisation for unprofitable high-multiple peers, while PANW itself was flat [10]. So I put 28% on full normalisation ($225, 45x), 49% on half normalisation ($350, 70x) and 23% on the premium persisting ($520, 99x). Scenario prices: probability-weighted mean $354. The ladder is a lognormal mixture with those medians and log-sigmas of 0.33/0.27/0.28. Overall log s.d. is ~0.42, below the 47% realized because 1Y vol includes a ~3x re-rating and 13-year monthly vol is 37% [8,9]. Ladder median ~$344, mean ~$369, P(>= spot) 0.31, P(<= fair value) ~0.25. Analyst average target $396 [7] is evidence only. Context only, in no number: the Goldman >20x EV/S base rate [37] and prediction-market odds [35,36]. Research limits: forward EV/EBITDA for peers is not available on a consistent basis, so it is null. SA shows only the current fiscal year's EPS, so each peer's next fiscal year is extrapolated with SA's 3Y EPS CAGR (cross-checked against Yahoo for CRWD and ZS [38,39]).
